terms.meaning: a way for a server to keep sending updates over one open web connection
one step in the replay, such as one incident

sections.name: File setup, limiter
sections.title: Setup and per-address limit
sections.what: Brings in the replay tools, the route helper, the limiter and the error type, and allows 30 replays per address per minute.
sections.why: Likely reason: each replay keeps a connection open, so requests are limited.

sections.name: sleep
sections.title: Replay stream handler
sections.what: Provides a short pause helper and streams the event's frames, starting after the resume position, at the requested speed.
sections.why: The pause helper lets the stream pace the frames so they arrive over time instead of all at once.
sections.watch_out: A speed value that is not a number is not rejected here, so it may produce odd timing.

summary: Streams a finished event's moments back to the page in order, at a chosen speed, as server-sent events.
purpose: Lets fans watch a past event unfold as if it were live.
why: Server-sent events keep one connection open so the page updates without asking again and again, and resuming from the last event id lets a dropped connection continue.
how: 1) Limits requests per address. 2) Reads the speed and resume position. 3) Loads the event's frames. 4) Streams them in order, pausing between them with the sleep helper.
inputs: A GET with the event id in the address, an optional speed value, and an optional resume position from the last event id header or the from parameter.
outputs: A stream of event messages with the event-stream content type.
risks: The speed value is not checked here, so a non-number or extreme value is passed on, and how the frame loader handles it is not visible.
debug: If the replay stops, check the connection and the resume position. If it runs too fast or slow, check the speed value and the frame timing.
